33: // CommitHook is an abstraction for executing arbitrary commands after atomic database commits
34: type CommitHook interface {
35: 	// Execute is arbitrary read-only function whose arguments are new Dataset commit into a specific Database.
36: 	// The returned values are a callback function and an error. The callback function is
37: 	// a Wait function which is optional. If returned, it will be registered with the ReplicationStatusController. If the
38: 	// hook implements NotifyWaitFailedCommitHook, it will be notified if the Wait function returns an error.
39: 	// The |Error| returned is actually ignored by the caller. It exists primarily for for unit testing. Any error which
40: 	// happens in a hook should be logged by the hook itself.
41: 	Execute(ctx context.Context, ds datas.Dataset, db *DoltDB) (func(context.Context) error, error)
42: 	// ExecuteForWorkingSets returns whether or not the hook should be executed for working set updates
43: 	ExecuteForWorkingSets() bool
44: 	// ExecuteForReplicaWrite returns whether or not the hook should be executed
45: 	// for writes received through the remotesapi endpoint as a cluster standby
46: 	// replica. Hooks like auto GC and stats should return true, while replication
47: 	// hooks (cluster replication, push-on-write) should return false to avoid
48: 	// replication loops.
49: 	ExecuteForReplicaWrite() bool
50: }
51: 
52: // NotifyWaitFailedCommitHook is an optional interface that can be implemented by CommitHooks.
53: // If a commit hook supports this interface, it can be notified if waiting for
54: // replication in the callback returned by |Execute| failed to complete in time
55: // or returned an error.
56: type NotifyWaitFailedCommitHook interface {
57: 	NotifyWaitFailed()
58: }

60: func (db hooksDatabase) SetCommitHooks(ctx context.Context, postHooks []CommitHook) hooksDatabase {
61: 	db.hooks = make([]CommitHook, len(postHooks))
62: 	copy(db.hooks, postHooks)
63: 	return db
64: }

72: 	toret := make([]CommitHook, len(db.hooks))
73: 	copy(toret, db.hooks)
74: 	return toret
75: }

77: func (db hooksDatabase) ExecuteCommitHooks(ctx context.Context, ds datas.Dataset, onlyWS bool, replicaWrite bool) {
78: 	var wg sync.WaitGroup
79: 	rsc := db.rsc
80: 	var ioff int
81: 	if rsc != nil {
82: 		ioff = len(rsc.Wait)
83: 		rsc.Wait = append(rsc.Wait, make([]func(context.Context) error, len(db.hooks))...)
84: 		rsc.NotifyWaitFailed = append(rsc.NotifyWaitFailed, make([]func(), len(db.hooks))...)
85: 	}
86: 	for il, hook := range db.hooks {
87: 		if (!onlyWS || hook.ExecuteForWorkingSets()) && (!replicaWrite || hook.ExecuteForReplicaWrite()) {
88: 			i := il
89: 			hook := hook
90: 			wg.Add(1)
91: 			go func() {
92: 				defer wg.Done()
93: 				// The error returned is intentionally ignored here. Hooks are expected to log errors themselves. The interface returns
94: 				// the error primarily for testing purposes.
95: 				f, _ := hook.Execute(ctx, ds, db.db)
96: 				if rsc != nil {
97: 					rsc.Wait[i+ioff] = f
98: 					if nf, ok := hook.(NotifyWaitFailedCommitHook); ok {
99: 						rsc.NotifyWaitFailed[i+ioff] = nf.NotifyWaitFailed
100: 					} else {
101: 						rsc.NotifyWaitFailed[i+ioff] = func() {}
102: 					}
103: 				}
104: 			}()
105: 		}
106: 	}
107: 	wg.Wait()
108: 	if rsc != nil {
109: 		j := ioff
110: 		for i := ioff; i < len(rsc.Wait); i++ {
111: 			// compact out any nil entries
112: 			if rsc.Wait[i] != nil {
113: 				rsc.Wait[j] = rsc.Wait[i]
114: 				rsc.NotifyWaitFailed[j] = rsc.NotifyWaitFailed[i]
115: 				j++
116: 			}
117: 		}
118: 		rsc.Wait = rsc.Wait[:j]
119: 		rsc.NotifyWaitFailed = rsc.NotifyWaitFailed[:j]
120: 	}
121: }

42: // Database provides versioned storage for noms values. While Values can be

44: // to read data by inspecting the Head of a Dataset and write new data by
45: // updating the Head of a Dataset via Commit() or similar. Particularly, new
46: // data is not guaranteed to be persistent until after a Commit (Delete,
47: // SetHeadToCommit, or FastForward) operation completes.
48: // The Database API is stateful, meaning that calls to GetDataset() or
49: // Datasets() occurring after a call to Commit() (et al) will represent the
50: // result of the Commit().

52: 	// Close must have no side-effects
53: 	io.Closer

55: 	// Datasets returns the root of the database which is a
56: 	// Map<String, Ref<Commit>> where string is a datasetID.

60: 	// datasetID in the above Datasets Map.

64: 	DatasetsByRootHash(ctx context.Context, rootHash hash.Hash) (DatasetsMap, error)
65:

67: 	// existed at the root hash given.
68: 	GetDatasetByRootHash(ctx context.Context, datasetID string, rootHash hash.Hash) (Dataset, error)
69: 
70: 	// BuildNewCommit creates a new Commit struct for the provided dataset,
71: 	// but does not modify the dataset. This allows the commit to be inspected
72: 	// if necessary before any update is performed.
73: 	BuildNewCommit(ctx context.Context, ds Dataset, v types.Value, opts CommitOptions) (*Commit, error)
74: 
75: 	// Commit updates the Commit that ds.ID() in this database points at. All
76: 	// Values that have been written to this Database are guaranteed to be
77: 	// persistent after Commit() returns successfully.
78: 	//
79: 	// The new Commit struct is constructed using v, opts.ParentsList, and
80: 	// opts.Meta. If opts.ParentsList is empty then the head value from
81: 	// |ds| is used as the parent. If opts.Meta is the zero value the
82: 	// Commit struct as an empty Meta struct.
83: 	//
84: 	// If the update cannot be performed because the existing dataset head
85: 	// is not a common ancestor of the constructed commit struct, returns

115: 	// already had a value, it must match the hash given or this method returns
116: 	// ErrOptimisticLockFailed and the caller must retry.

123: 	// pessimistic lock that UpdateWorkingSet does, asserting that the hash |prevWsHash| given is still the current one
124: 	// before attempting to write a new value. And it does the normal optimistic locking that Commit does, assuming the

126: 	// updated in the new root, or neither of them are.

251: func (r fbRvStorage) serializeRootValue(addressMapBytes []byte, dbSchemas []schema.DatabaseSchema) (*serial.RootValue, error) {
252: 	builder := flatbuffers.NewBuilder(80)
253: 	tablesoff := builder.CreateByteVector(addressMapBytes)
254: 	schemasOff := serializeDatabaseSchemas(builder, dbSchemas)
255: 
256: 	fkoff := builder.CreateByteVector(r.srv.ForeignKeyAddrBytes())
257: 	serial.RootValueStart(builder)
258: 	serial.RootValueAddFeatureVersion(builder, r.srv.FeatureVersion())
259: 	serial.RootValueAddCollation(builder, r.srv.Collation())
260: 	serial.RootValueAddTables(builder, tablesoff)
261: 	serial.RootValueAddForeignKeyAddr(builder, fkoff)
262: 	if schemasOff > 0 {
263: 		serial.RootValueAddSchemas(builder, schemasOff)
264: 	}
265: 
266: 	bs := serial.FinishMessage(builder, serial.RootValueEnd(builder), []byte(serial.RootValueFileID))
267: 	msg, err := serial.TryGetRootAsRootValue(bs, serial.MessagePrefixSz)
268: 	if err != nil {
269: 		return nil, err
270: 	}
271: 	return msg, nil
272: }

274: func serializeDatabaseSchemas(b *flatbuffers.Builder, dbSchemas []schema.DatabaseSchema) flatbuffers.UOffsetT {
275: 	// if we have no schemas, do not serialize an empty vector
276: 	if len(dbSchemas) == 0 {
277: 		return 0
278: 	}
279: 
280: 	offsets := make([]flatbuffers.UOffsetT, len(dbSchemas))
281: 	for i := len(dbSchemas) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
282: 		dbSchema := dbSchemas[i]
283: 
284: 		nameOff := b.CreateString(dbSchema.Name)
285: 		serial.DatabaseSchemaStart(b)
286: 		serial.DatabaseSchemaAddName(b, nameOff)
287: 		offsets[i] = serial.DatabaseSchemaEnd(b)
288: 	}
289: 
290: 	serial.RootValueStartSchemasVector(b, len(offsets))
291: 	for i := len(offsets) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
292: 		b.PrependUOffsetT(offsets[i])
293: 	}
294: 	return b.EndVector(len(offsets))
295: }

297: // encodeTableNameForSerialization encodes a table name for serialization. Table names with no schema are encoded as
298: // just the bare table name. Table names with schemas are encoded by surrounding the schema name with null bytes and
299: // appending the table name.
300: func encodeTableNameForSerialization(name TableName) string {
301: 	if name.Schema == "" {
302: 		return name.Name
303: 	}
304: 	return fmt.Sprintf("\000%s\000%s", name.Schema, name.Name)

308: // |encodeTableNameForSerialization|
309: func decodeTableNameFromSerialization(encodedName string) (TableName, bool) {
310: 	if len(encodedName) == 0 {
311: 		return TableName{}, false
312: 	}
313: 
314: 	if encodedName[0] != 0 {
315: 		return TableName{Name: encodedName}, true
316: 	} else if len(encodedName) >= 4 { // 2 null bytes plus at least one char for schema and table name
317: 		schemaEnd := strings.LastIndexByte(encodedName, 0)
318: 		return TableName{
319: 			Schema: encodedName[1:schemaEnd],
320: 			Name:   encodedName[schemaEnd+1:],
321: 		}, true
322: 	}
323: 
324: 	// invalid encoding
325: 	return TableName{}, false
326: }

334: 		len(encodedName) > len(schemaName)+2 &&
335: 		encodedName[1:len(schemaName)+1] == schemaName {

190: func doltCommit(ctx *sql.Context,
191: 	dbName string,

195: 	commit *doltdb.PendingCommit, // optional
196: 	workingSet *doltdb.WorkingSet, // must be provided
197: 	currHash hash.Hash, // hash of the current working set to be written

199: ) (*doltdb.WorkingSet, *doltdb.Commit, error) {
200: 	pending := *commit
201: 
202: 	headRef, err := workingSet.Ref().ToHeadRef()
203: 	if err != nil {
204: 		return nil, nil, err
205: 	}
206: 
207: 	headSpec, _ := doltdb.NewCommitSpec("HEAD")
208: 	optCmt, err := doltDb.Resolve(ctx, headSpec, headRef)
209: 	if err != nil {
210: 		return nil, nil, err
211: 	}
212: 	curHead, ok := optCmt.ToCommit()
213: 	if !ok {
214: 		return nil, nil, doltdb.ErrGhostCommitRuntimeFailure
215: 	}
216: 
217: 	// We already got a new staged root via merge or ff via the doCommit method, so now apply it to the STAGED value
218: 	// we're about to commit.
219: 	pending.Roots.Staged = workingSet.StagedRoot()
220: 
221: 	// We check if the branch HEAD has changed since our transaction started and perform an additional merge if so. The
222: 	// non-dolt-commit transaction logic only merges working sets and doesn't consider the HEAD value.
223: 	if curHead != nil {
224: 		curRootVal, err := curHead.ResolveRootValue(ctx)
225: 		if err != nil {
226: 			return nil, nil, err
227: 		}
228: 		curRootValHash, err := curRootVal.HashOf()
229: 		if err != nil {
230: 			return nil, nil, err
231: 		}
232: 		headRootValHash, err := pending.Roots.Head.HashOf()
233: 		if err != nil {
234: 			return nil, nil, err
235: 		}
236: 
237: 		if curRootValHash != headRootValHash {
238: 			// If the branch head changed since our transaction started, then we merge
239: 			// the existing branch head (curRootVal) into our staged root value. We
240: 			// treat the HEAD of the branch when our transaction started as the common
241: 			// ancestor (TODO: This will not be true in the case of destructive branch
242: 			// updates). The merged root value becomes our new Staged root value which
243: 			// is the value which we are trying to commit.
244: 			start := time.Now()
245: 
246: 			tableResolver, err := GetTableResolver(ctx, dbName)
247: 			if err != nil {
248: 				return nil, nil, err
249: 			}
250: 			result, err := merge.MergeRoots(
251: 				ctx,
252: 				tableResolver,
253: 				pending.Roots.Staged,
254: 				curRootVal,
255: 				pending.Roots.Head,
256: 				curHead,
257: 				startState,
258: 				mergeOpts,
259: 				merge.MergeOpts{})
260: 			if err != nil {
261: 				return nil, nil, err
262: 			}
263: 			pending.Roots.Staged = result.Root
264: 
265: 			// We also need to update the working set to reflect the new staged root value
266: 			workingSet = workingSet.WithStagedRoot(pending.Roots.Staged)
267: 
268: 			logrus.Tracef("staged and HEAD merge took %s", time.Since(start))
269: 		}
270: 	}

272: 	workingSet = workingSet.ClearMerge()

274: 	name, email, _, _, err := ResolveNameEmail(ctx, DoltCommitterName, DoltCommitterEmail)
275: 	if err != nil {
276: 		return nil, nil, err
277: 	}
278: 
279: 	var rsc doltdb.ReplicationStatusController
280: 	newCommit, err := doltDb.CommitWithWorkingSet(ctx, headRef, workingSet.Ref(), &pending, workingSet, currHash, tx.WorkingSetMeta(name, email), &rsc)

317: func WaitForReplicationController(ctx *sql.Context, rsc doltdb.ReplicationStatusController) {
318: 	if len(rsc.Wait) == 0 {
319: 		return
320: 	}
321: 	_, timeout, ok := sql.SystemVariables.GetGlobal(DoltClusterAckWritesTimeoutSecs)
322: 	if !ok {
323: 		return
324: 	}
325: 	timeoutI := timeout.(int64)
326: 	if timeoutI == 0 {
327: 		return
328: 	}
329: 
330: 	cCtx, cancel := context.WithCancelCause(ctx)
331: 	var wg sync.WaitGroup
332: 	wg.Add(len(rsc.Wait))
333: 	for i, f := range rsc.Wait {
334: 		f := f
335: 		i := i
336: 		go func() {
337: 			defer wg.Done()
338: 			err := f(cCtx)
339: 			if err == nil {
340: 				rsc.Wait[i] = nil
341: 			}
342: 		}()
343: 	}
344: 
345: 	done := make(chan struct{})
346: 	go func() {
347: 		wg.Wait()
348: 		close(done)
349: 	}()
350: 
351: 	waitFailed := false
352: 	select {
353: 	case <-time.After(time.Duration(timeoutI) * time.Second):
354: 		// We timed out before all the waiters were done.
355: 		// First we make certain to finalize everything.
356: 		cancel(doltdb.ErrReplicationWaitFailed)
357: 		<-done
358: 		waitFailed = true
359: 	case <-done:
360: 		cancel(context.Canceled)
361: 	}
362: 
363: 	// Just because our waiters all completed does not mean they all
364: 	// returned nil errors. Any non-nil entries in rsc.Wait returned an
365: 	// error. We turn those into warnings here.
366: 	numFailed := 0
367: 	for i, f := range rsc.Wait {
368: 		if f != nil {
369: 			numFailed += 1
370: 			if waitFailed {
371: 				rsc.NotifyWaitFailed[i]()
372: 			}
373: 		}
374: 	}
375: 	if numFailed > 0 {
376: 		ctx.Session.Warn(&sql.Warning{
377: 			Level:   "Warning",
378: 			Code:    mysql.ERQueryTimeout,
379: 			Message: fmt.Sprintf("Timed out replication of commit to %d out of %d replicas.", numFailed, len(rsc.Wait)),

93: // fires the DoltDB's registered CommitHooks for every ref-typed dataset whose
94: // head address changed between |last| and |current|.
95: func (s hooksFiringRemoteSrvStore) Commit(ctx context.Context, current, last hash.Hash) (bool, error) {
96: 	// Snapshot old dataset head addresses before the commit.
97: 	oldDatasets, _ := s.ddb.DatasetsByRootHash(ctx, last)
98: 
99: 	ok, err := s.RemoteSrvStore.Commit(ctx, current, last)
100: 	if !ok || err != nil {
101: 		return ok, err
102: 	}
103: 
104: 	// Snapshot new dataset head addresses after the successful commit.
105: 	newDatasets, err := s.ddb.DatasetsByRootHash(ctx, current)
106: 	if err != nil {
107: 		// Don't fail the commit; hooks are best-effort.
108: 		return true, nil
109: 	}
110: 
111: 	// Build lookup maps for both old and new dataset head addresses.
112: 	oldAddrs := make(map[string]hash.Hash)
113: 	if oldDatasets != nil {
114: 		_ = oldDatasets.IterAll(ctx, func(id string, addr hash.Hash) error {
115: 			oldAddrs[id] = addr
116: 			return nil
117: 		})
118: 	}
119: 	newAddrs := make(map[string]hash.Hash)
120: 	_ = newDatasets.IterAll(ctx, func(id string, addr hash.Hash) error {
121: 		newAddrs[id] = addr
122: 		return nil
123: 	})
124: 
125: 	executeHooks := s.ddb.ExecuteCommitHooks
126: 	if s.replicaWrite {
127: 		executeHooks = s.ddb.ExecuteReplicaCommitHooks
128: 	}
129: 
130: 	// Fire hooks for each ref-typed dataset that was added or changed.
131: 	for id, newAddr := range newAddrs {
132: 		if !ref.IsRef(id) {
133: 			continue
134: 		}
135: 		if oldAddr, existed := oldAddrs[id]; !existed || oldAddr != newAddr {
136: 			_ = executeHooks(ctx, id)
137: 		}
138: 	}
139: 
140: 	// Fire hooks for each ref-typed dataset that was deleted.
141: 	for id := range oldAddrs {
142: 		if !ref.IsRef(id) {
143: 			continue
144: 		}
145: 		if _, exists := newAddrs[id]; !exists {
146: 			_ = executeHooks(ctx, id)
147: 		}
148: 	}

160: func (c *AutoGCController) gcBgThread(ctx context.Context) {
161: 	var wg sync.WaitGroup
162: 	runCh := make(chan autoGCWork)
163: 	wg.Add(1)
164: 	go func() {
165: 		defer wg.Done()
166: 		dbs := make([]autoGCWork, 0)
167: 		// Accumulate GC requests, only one will come in per database at a time.
168: 		// Send the oldest one out to the worker when it is ready.
169: 		for {
170: 			var toSendCh chan autoGCWork
171: 			var toSend autoGCWork
172: 			if len(dbs) > 0 {
173: 				toSend = dbs[0]
174: 				toSendCh = runCh
175: 			}
176: 
177: 			select {
178: 			case <-ctx.Done():
179: 				// sql.BackgroundThreads is shutting down.
180: 				// No need to drain or anything; just
181: 				// return.
182: 				return
183: 			case newDB := <-c.workCh:
184: 				dbs = append(dbs, newDB)
185: 			case toSendCh <- toSend:
186: 				// We just sent the front of the slice.
187: 				// Delete it from our set of pending GCs.
188: 				copy(dbs[:], dbs[1:])
189: 				dbs = dbs[:len(dbs)-1]
190: 			}
191: 
192: 		}
193: 	}()
194: 	wg.Add(1)
195: 	go func() {
196: 		defer wg.Done()
197: 		for {
198: 			select {
199: 			case <-ctx.Done():
200: 				return
201: 			case work := <-runCh:
202: 				if err := c.scheduler.WaitForNextRun(ctx); err != nil {
203: 					return
204: 				}
205: 				c.doWork(ctx, work, c.ctxF)
